author: tfireubs-ui
body:
## Problem

The `pendingNonces` and `pendingNonceTimestamps` Maps in `builder.ts` have no size bound. In long-running processes cycling through many addresses (multi-wallet, testing), these grow unboundedly.

## Solution

Add a `MAX_PENDING_NONCES = 100` cap with oldest-first eviction in `advancePendingNonce()`.

When the map exceeds the cap after a new entry is added, the entry with the oldest timestamp is evicted from both maps.

## Why oldest-first

Addresses not seen recently are most likely to be inactive — evicting them first preserves the working set for active addresses.

Closes #336

author: gaborbernat
body:
Downstream packagers (Debian) reported several problems with the tox manpage introduced in #1409. The RST title block and field-list metadata created a malformed top section where `SYNOPSIS` and other headings were indented under an unwanted parent section. Both `man_pages` config and the RST source generated their own `AUTHOR` and `COPYRIGHT` sections, producing duplicates. The `project` variable was never set in `conf.py`, causing `"Project name not set"` to appear in the manpage header. Finally, `shared-data` shipped the raw `.rst` source file rather than a compiled troff manpage, so `tox man` and `man tox` never worked.

The RST header block is removed since `man_pages` already handles the title, section, and description. The `AUTHOR` section is kept only in the RST (with the GitHub link) while clearing the `man_pages` authors list to prevent duplication. The `COPYRIGHT` section is removed from the RST since Sphinx generates one from `conf.py`. Setting `project = name` fixes the header. A hatch build hook using docutils now compiles the manpage to troff format at wheel-build time, so pip, pipx, and `uv tool install` all get a working `tox.1` -- and `tox man` can find and symlink it correctly.

Fixes #3878

### Motivation

- Make fresh multi-run preflop solves deterministic across repeated requests and speed them up by running independent runs in parallel while preserving previous cancellation/fallback behavior.

### Description

- Replace the serial per-run loop in `RunFreshMultiRunTraining` with a parallel execution that computes per-run seeds from `ComputeDeterministicFreshSolveBaseSeed` and runs `ExecuteFreshRun` for each seed. 
- Add `ExecuteFreshRun` and the `FreshRunResult` record to encapsulate per-run outputs, and add `ComputeDeterministicFreshSolveBaseSeed` and `AccumulateHash` to produce a stable base seed from request data. 
- Aggregate only completed runs, average policies/regrets/weights and build aggregated in-memory stores, and handle cancellation by returning whatever runs completed (with a uniform fallback when none completed). 
- Preserve elapsed/iteration aggregation and action-value averaging logic and ensure the current policy falls back to `UniformPolicyBuilder.Build` when missing.

author: recharte
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive overhaul of the CI/CD pipeline and integration testing infrastructure. The main improvements include a modernized and modular GitHub Actions workflow for CI, reusable integration test workflows using k3d and kuttl, and new Makefile targets to support these workflows. It also removes the old copyright workflow and improves the dev image publishing process.

**CI/CD Pipeline Modernization:**

- Introduced a new `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` that consolidates build, verification, copyright, Helm lint, and integration test jobs, using a matrix and job dependencies for efficiency. Integration tests are split into core and sharded suites and run via a reusable workflow.
- Added `.github/workflows/integration-test.yaml`, a reusable workflow for running kuttl test suites inside a k3d cluster, supporting both core and sharded integration tests.
- Added `.github/actions/setup-k8s-tools/action.yaml` to install k3d, kuttl, and kubectl with checksum verification, ensuring consistent tool versions in CI.

**Build and Publish Improvements:**

- Refactored and renamed the dev image build workflow to `.github/workflows/publish.yaml`, improving caching, artifact handling, and manifest creation. Added support for manual workflow dispatch and increased robustness of multi-arch builds.

**Makefile Enhancements:**

- Added variables and targets to support integration testing in k3d, including `test-integration-core`, `test-integration-sharded`, `load-image`, `install-crds`, and `deploy-provider-ci`. This enables seamless local and CI testing workflows.

**Test Suite Configuration:**

- Added `test/integration/kuttl-core.yaml` and `test/integration/kuttl-sharded.yaml` to define kuttl test suites for core and sharded MongoDB topologies, aligning with the new Makefile and CI workflows.

**Cleanup and Removal:**

- Removed the legacy `.github/workflows/copyright.yml` in favor of a simpler, non-pushing check in the new CI workflow.

These changes collectively bring the project’s CI, testing, and build infrastructure up to date, improve reliability, and make it easier to extend and maintain.

`basl new --scaffold myapp` creates an app with example module and test:
- `lib/<name>.basl` - module with `greet()` function
- `test/<name>_test.basl` - test that imports and tests the module  
- `main.basl` - imports and uses the module

Helps users remember module import and test patterns.

### Add --output option
`basl new -o /path/to/dir myapp` creates the project in a specific directory.

## Usage
```bash
basl new myapp                      # Create in current directory
basl new --scaffold myapp           # With example module and test
basl new -o ~/projects myapp        # Create in specific directory
basl new -o ~/projects -s myapp     # Combine options
```

When a CI job re-runs, its table rows in the PR beacon comment were previously removed and appended at the end, causing row ordering to change on every re-run. This adds a `replaceMode` option that controls row positioning during updates:

- `'in-place'` (new default): new rows replace at the position of the first matching old row, preserving ordering
- `'append'`: old behavior — remove all old rows and append new ones at end

author: ben-malbeclabs
body:
## Summary

RFC-18 introduces a link classification model for DoubleZero using IS-IS Flexible Algorithm (flex-algo). DZF assigns named topology labels to links onchain; the controller translates these into IS-IS TE admin-groups and flex-algo topology definitions on Arista EOS devices. BGP color extended communities steer VPN unicast traffic onto constrained topologies, while IP multicast continues to resolve via IS-IS algo 0 across all links.

**New onchain accounts and fields:**
- `TopologyInfo` PDA — foundation-managed; defines a constrained IS-IS forwarding plane with auto-assigned admin-group bit (from a new `AdminGroupBits` `ResourceExtension`), flex-algo number, and derived EOS color (`admin_group_bit + 1`); supports `include-any` and `exclude` constraints
- `link_topologies: Vec<Pubkey>` on `Link` — assigns topologies to a link; auto-set to UNICAST-DEFAULT at activation; foundation-only write; capped at 8 entries
- `unicast_drained: bool` on `Link` — contributor-writable capacity management tool; when true, controller appends the UNICAST-DRAINED admin-group to the interface, excluding the link from all constrained unicast topologies without affecting multicast (algo 0) or modifying permanent topology tags
- `include_topologies: Vec<Pubkey>` on `Tenant` — foundation-only; assigns specific topologies for per-tenant path differentiation via BGP color extended communities; defaults to color 1 (UNICAST-DEFAULT) if unset
- `flex_algo_node_segments: Vec<FlexAlgoNodeSegment>` on `Interface` — one `(topology: Pubkey, node_segment_idx: u16)` entry per active topology per Vpnv4 loopback; allocated at activation and automatically backfilled across all existing loopbacks when a new topology is created

**UNICAST-DRAINED:**
A controller-managed admin-group alias (bit pre-marked in `AdminGroupBits` at program initialization). Always defined on all devices. `exclude 1` always injected into every `include-any` flex-algo definition — structural, not conditional on any link being drained. Draining a link removes it from all constrained unicast topologies for all tenants simultaneously; multicast is unaffected.

**Controller:**
- New `features.yaml` config file (`-features-config` flag) — `enabled` gates topology config and link admin-group tagging; `community_stamping` provides granular per-tenant and per-device control over BGP color community stamping for staged rollout
- Full revert: `enabled: false` removes all flex-algo config from all devices on the next reconciliation cycle
- Startup check: blocks `enabled: true` if any Vpnv4 loopback has an empty `flex_algo_node_segments` list; directs operator to run migration

**Migration:**
One-time `doublezero-admin` CLI command to tag existing links with UNICAST-DEFAULT and populate `flex_algo_node_segments` on existing Vpnv4 loopbacks. Idempotent, with `--dry-run` support.

body:
## Summary
This change adds websocket authentication at the app-server transport boundary and enforces it before JSON-RPC `initialize`, so authenticated deployments reject unauthenticated clients during the websocket handshake rather than after a connection has already been admitted.

During rollout, websocket auth is opt-in for non-loopback listeners so we do not break existing remote clients. If `--ws-auth ...` is configured, the server enforces auth during websocket upgrade. If auth is not configured, non-loopback listeners still start, but app-server logs a warning and the startup banner calls out that auth should be configured before real remote use.

The server supports two auth modes: a file-backed capability token, and a standard HMAC-signed JWT/JWS bearer token verified with the `jsonwebtoken` crate, with optional issuer, audience, and clock-skew validation. Capability tokens are normalized, hashed, and compared in constant time. Short shared secrets for signed bearer tokens are rejected at startup. Requests carrying an `Origin` header are rejected with `403` by transport middleware, and authenticated clients present credentials as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` during websocket upgrade.

## Validation
- `cargo test -p codex-app-server transport::auth`
- `cargo test -p codex-cli app_server_`
- `cargo clippy -p codex-app-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`

`--extended` could emit a generic capability warning that was ambiguous for Solana and suggested extended data might be missing. This PR makes that warning Solana-aware and aligns the docs/tests with the actual mapper behavior: Solana extended mode can emit `vote_transactions` even when endpoint feature advertisement is absent.

- **Warning semantics**
  - Special-cases Solana in `resolve_extended_mode` warning text.
  - Reframes the message as an endpoint capability-advertisement mismatch, not a definitive statement that extended Solana output is unavailable.
  - Keeps `--extended` as the only switch that enables extended output; no behavior change to mapper selection.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Adds targeted tests for Solana chain-name detection and warning text selection.
  - Preserves the generic warning for non-Solana chains.

- **Docs alignment**
  - Updates CLI/help text in the README to reflect that `--extended` is not EVM-only.
  - Expands the Solana table summary to include current base tables and the extended-only `vote_transactions` table.

```rust
fn extended_warning_message(endpoint_info: &Option<EndpointInfo>) -> &'static str {
    if endpoint_info.as_ref().is_some_and(|ei| {

    } else {
        "--extended requested but endpoint did not advertise extended block features"
    }
}
```

## Summary
Critical reliability fixes to prevent zombie processes, hung async contexts, and duplicate instance spawning.

### Changes
- **SIGKILL fallback**: `close()` now sends SIGTERM with a configurable grace period (`WEAVE_KILL_GRACE_MS`, default 5s), then escalates to SIGKILL if the process hasn't exited. Prevents zombie child processes when opencode hangs on SIGTERM.
- **Subscribe timeout**: `client.event.subscribe()` calls in `session-status-watcher.ts` and `callback-monitor.ts` are wrapped in `Promise.race` with a configurable timeout (`WEAVE_SUBSCRIBE_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 30s). Prevents permanently stuck async contexts when the SDK hangs.
- **Spawn mutex**: Added per-directory async deduplication lock to `spawnInstance()` using a `Map<string, Promise<ManagedInstance>>`. Concurrent `POST /api/sessions` for the same directory now coalesce into a single spawn instead of racing.

Based on the KRAM whitepaper, this PR adds a draft implementation of dynamic cache-type configuration updates for Kramer, including:

- Case 1: pure decrease of the window along with pruning which is immediate.
- Case 2: increase of the window, pruning immediately changes while window changes are staged.
- Test covering: increase, decrease, existing cache immutability, new cache with updated values 

Case 3 hasn't been implemented (see https://github.com/SmithSamuelM/Papers/blob/master/whitepapers/kram.md#changing-the-cache-type-database) 

Notes/up for discussion:

- The update is done by updating cf and passing the new cf through .changeConfig() which is a new function of the Kramer class. 
- All pending changes are kept inside a set in kramer in memory, not in a db
- The new reconcileConfig() function checks if delta (where delta = new accept lag - old accept lag) has passed so the cache-type values can be updated without creating any gaps. Currently it is manually being called, I thought it could possibly be called inside processMsg() or inside a doer that runs periodically. The best case scenario would be to time it so it runs once exactly after delta has passed. 
- Drift (d) is preserved for now

## Summary

Embedding endpoint (`/v1/embeddings`) only supports 6 hardcoded cloud providers. Local inference backends (oMLX, Ollama) serving embeddings via provider_nodes are inaccessible through OmniRoute.

### Changes (3 files, ~85 lines)

- **`open-sse/config/embeddingRegistry.ts`** — Export `EmbeddingProvider` interface, add `buildDynamicEmbeddingProvider()` with input validation (prefix, baseUrl, no `/` in prefix), add Phase 2 provider_nodes fallback in `parseEmbeddingModel()`, type `getEmbeddingProvider()`

- Only localhost providers (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost) — prevents auth bypass and SSRF

author: antoinetue
body:
This PR aims to provide more flexibility and improved quality for export of (mainly) graphs from the toolbox.
As it stands we offer limited export options (only png to clipboard as of 412e346), with no real control over the styling.

While it would be hard to compete with a handcrafted matplotlib figure, *some* level of adjustment over the styling, and support of vector formats are essential for creating plots to share, present, or even publish.

## Overview
In short, this PR: 

* Implements two custom exporters
  *  A custom matplotlib exporter
  * A custom file exporter
*  Re-enables the right-click export menu, reverting 412e346
* Removes unused/unwanted pyqtgraph exporters, in favour of the custom exporters
  * Matplotlib exporter
  * HDF5 exporter
  * CSV exporter
* ~Adds a dialog to 'export graph to clipboard' to prompt the user for a style~

After in-person discussion (see also comments):

* the custom matplotlib exporter can export to clipboard (using its config), no more dialog popups needed. 
* Support two styles when saving plot data to text file: 
  * `Export`: a flat column layout, simpler to read in external programs
  * `Save`:  uses a pandas multi index to preserve hierarchy of files/ROIs better
* storing excel/parquet always uses multi index, so no difference between save/export



## Custom exporters

The file exporter is rather simple: through the export dialog, the user can pick the desired kind of export (spectra, NIST table, Molecule fit table, continuum fit table).
When exporting, the appropriate export action is triggered from the toolbox main window menu, the rest of the process is thus identical.

The matplotlib exporter replaces the default pyqtgraph version.
In the export dialog, it is possible to set a DPI for the file, as well as adjust some legend settings to help in legibility and appearance (shortening names and handles, explicitly setting legend position). 
Further (advanced) customization can be applied through one or more matplotlib stylesheets, which can be selected.
The bundled stylesheet is selected by default at first, but any style that is available systemwide can be used.
This allow e.g. using a seaborn style, or a users custom style(s). 
By applying multiple different stylesheets on top of each other, quite a bit of control over the styling can be achieved. 
Finally, visibility of a plot item (controlled by the pyqtgraph legend) is now also respected, meaning a plotted, but hidden(!) item will no longer be exported.
The result will be a matplotlib window opening, allowing some simple, final adjustments to the plot, which can then be saved to several formats. 

## Export dialog & removed exporters

The CSVExporter, HDF5Exporter and MatplotlibExporter from pyqtgraph are deregistered at runtime, to avoid them being used over the custom ones.
Since they will not show up as options anymore, the right-click menu to export can be shown once more for the graph.

The ImageExporter and SVGExporter are left operational, since they will export the pyqtgraph version of the graph, which may be desired by some. 

## Potential regression

~Exporting to clipboard now asks the user to select a single stylesheet to apply before exporting, meaning it requires one (accept) or two (pick&accept) more actions than before.
An alternative could be to handle this through the custom MatplotlibExporter, picking the currently active choices, without showing a dialog.
The fact that the plot style could be controlled via the right-click menu in that case would be not obvious however, I think.~
No more  dialog needed to adjust styling, the settings of the right-click export dialog are used
